clips.title: The story
paras: Je'neu Sancrea at Zoram'gar Outpost has noticed the naga of Blackfathom Deeps harvesting potent sapphire clusters from the caverns. Concerned by their magical properties and elemental water energies, the shaman tasks Horde adventurers with recovering the gems before they can be misused.

On the mist-shrouded shores of the Zoram Strand, the Darkspear shaman Je'neu Sancrea keeps watch over ancient Kaldorei ruins now overrun by sinister forces. Deep within the submerged chambers of Blackfathom Deeps, naga have begun mining vibrant sapphire formations that sprout along the damp cavern walls. Sensing that the serpentine invaders seek to harness this volatile power, Sancrea seeks to intercept the harvest before their designs can come to fruition.

The Sapphires of Aku'mai are far more than ordinary gemstones; they thrum with elemental resonance and harbor clinging water spirits. In the hands of adept sorcerers, such conduits could fuel dangerous arcane rituals or amplify the influence of the shadowy hydra, Aku'mai, whose dark presence permeates the subterranean temple. Recovering these clusters deprives the naga of an invaluable reagent and safeguards the coastline from runaway elemental magic.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: Within the beginning tunnels of Blackfathom Deeps, large sapphire clusters can be found along the cave walls. Recently it was noted that the naga were harvesting the crystals. Until it can be discerned why, I sense we should stop the naga from succeeding. The crystals have great elemental power and if used inappropriately, could make for a powerful arcane component.
Will you help me, friend? Blackfathom Deeps can be found along Zoram Strand to the north of our outpost.

clips.title: Progress
paras: How goes your search for the crystals, friend? Have you witnessed the naga harvesting them? I pray to my ancestors we find the reason they are collecting such things.

clips.title: Completion
paras: Well done, friend. These are the crystals I spoke of. Intriguing...
I can feel the power within them. The spirits of water cling to them. Whatever the naga were going to use these for... Well, let us be glad they are no longer in their hands.
